note: From the original English description by Hill 1922 (the original labelled Hamitermes eucalypti sp. n., later placed in Amitermes); this entry is written from the alate description, the soldier being treated separately in the same work (the original gives the soldier head in frontal and lateral view in fig. 25, with the description following in the text). The measurement ranges are from the type series. In the OCR the hyphen "-" stands in the measurements for either a decimal point or a range, and has been restored here to decimal points and dashes according to the context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original was published as the new species Hamitermes eucalypti. The alate wing surface is densely covered with fine hairs; the radius and radial sector, the base of the media and the first 7—8 branches of the cubitus are distinct, the cubital branches sometimes anastomosing to form wing cells; the abdomen has 10 dark tergites, the first 8 each with a small pale spot.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Abdomen long, nearly cylindrical, with 10 dark tergites, the first 8 each distinct and each with a small pale spot near the lateral margin, moderately hairy; sternites 8 distinct, pale, each with a dark spot on the lateral margins only, sternite 6 longest and darkest; in the male sternites 7 distinct, the first 3 with lateral spots, the rest nearly concolorous, the venter darker than in the female; cerci short, the basal and apical segments equal in length. Measurements: length with wings 11—12, without wings 6.5—8; head including mandibles 1.2—1.3, width including compound eyes 1.1; right mandible length 0.6—0.62, width 0.46, left mandible length 0.65—0.67, width 0.35—0.37; antenna length 1.65; pronotum length 0.47, width 0.98; fore and hind wing length 9.25; forewing width 2.58, hindwing width 2.68; tibiae (i) 0.7—0.75, (ii) 0.8, (iii) 1.1—1.13; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.
